text: Sampling theory says a signal with no frequencies above f can be reconstructed from samples taken faster than 2f. What is remarkable about that?
choices: The reconstruction is exact, not approximate — discreteness need not lose information
It applies only to audio and not to images
It proves analogue recording is always better
It means any sampling rate is sufficient
explanation: The Nyquist-Shannon result is much stronger than 'close enough': a continuous wave can be recovered exactly from discrete instants, provided you know what it does not contain. Sampling too slowly gives aliasing, where high frequencies masquerade as low ones — the wagon-wheel effect.
